question.problem: A summer camp has capacity for $200$ kids. The price for each kid attending the camp is $$300.$ The cost of setting up the camp is made up of a fixed cost of $$2\,000$ plus a cost of $$100$ per kid. How many kids should attend the summer camp to maximize its profit?
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we apply the candidates test.

First, note that for $x$ kids attending, the summer camp has a revenue (in dollars) of 

$$
R(x)=300\cdot x=300x
$$

and a cost (in dollars) of 

$$
C(x)={{2\,000}_{⏟}}_{\text{fixed cost}}\,\,+{{100x.}_{⏟}}_{\text{variable cost}}
$$

Therefore, the profit function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x) & =R(x)-C(x) \\  & =300x-(2\,000+100x) \\  & =200x-2\,000.\end{aligned}
$$

We note that the permitted domain is $0\le x\le 200.$ Therefore, $x=0$ and $x=200$ are candidates for the global maxima of $P(x).$

We need to find the critical points of $P(x)$ for $0<x<200.$ Taking the derivative, we get

$$
{P}^{′}(x)=200.
$$

We can see that the equation ${P}^{′}(x)=0$ has no solutions.

Thus, our candidates are $x=0$ and $x=200.$ Computing $P(x)$ at each of these values, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0) & =200(0)-2\,000=-2\,000 \\ P(200) & =200(200)-2\,000=38\,000\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the summer camp will have a maximum profit level when $200$ kids attend.
